recommendation: Keep this source fix as-is. It is a narrow build-scope correction that restores the published terminology decision after a later wording addition; no broader workflow terminology sweep is recommended from this issue alone.
issue_request: FHIR-11435 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I change request against the DSTU2 workflow page asking that workflow uses of "intermediary" be replaced with "queue server" or another clearer term, because REST intermediaries are usually transparent infrastructure rather than message-queue-like servers.
initial_application: The Jira records svn @10162 as the application. In git, 83f1205cc1f012816734622c56ee12d93a24212d includes #11435 and replaced the old source/workflow.html workflow pattern uses of "intermediary" with "queue server" in the decision question, option headings, steps, benefits, limitations, and recommendations. The later GF#11492 split moved that corrected workflow content into current workflow pages.
additional_context: The current workflow communication page is in build scope through source/hierarchy.xml. Later commit 86c92a8842624a25700fdcee18308d8971c039d2 added a new Communication Pattern Considerations paragraph that again used "intermediary" for a third-party system holding workflow records. The remaining workflow uses of "intermediary/broker" describe an actual broker pattern, and the "Intermediary consultation note available" table cell is unrelated to the queue-server terminology decision. Community and Confluence searches found no conflicting evidence.
reconciliation: Changed source/workflow-communications.html so the current Communication Pattern Considerations paragraph refers to "queue server or broker" instead of the ambiguous generic "intermediary", preserving the original FHIR-11435 intent while not changing the separate broker-specific pattern.
source_changes: source/workflow-communications.html: Replaced "placer, filler or intermediary" with "placer, filler, queue server or broker" in the Communication Pattern Considerations paragraph.
